page: Hetzner Cloud ccx43 is a dedicated general purpose cloud instance built on AMD EPYC x86_64 processors virtualized via QEMU. The configuration provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz, supporting simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 62.0 GB of RAM, equating to roughly 3.91 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled directly with a 360 GB NVMe SSD, while no discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread execution, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2022.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3015.99, both ranking in the top 25 percent. Text processing stands out in the top 10 percent with a Geekbench score of 2905.0. Multi-core operations register in the middle tier, recording 12245.0 in Geekbench multi-core, 24391.96 in stress-ng multi-core, and a PassMark CPU score of 27151.63. Memory throughput measures 62.67 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 48.85 GB/sec for uncached write operations.

Application and synthetic throughput metrics confirm solid mid-range performance for transactional systems, reaching 20.97 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and 14.54 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Light language modeling workloads show responsive execution with 306.44 tokens per second on small 135M parameter models, whereas heavy 70B parameter models show constrained prompt processing at 4.03 tokens per second. Dedicated core reservations avoid noisy neighbor interference, providing stable compute density relative to overall resource capacity.

With its 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio, integrated fast NVMe storage, and reliable single-thread efficiency, Hetzner Cloud ccx43 fits production workloads such as relational databases, backend web serving, continuous integration builds, and data transformation pipelines.

The system provides 62.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.91 GB per vCPU, accompanied by a bundled 360 GB local NVMe SSD without discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight strong single-core compute performance, placing in the top 25 percent for single-threaded stress-ng and Geekbench tests, alongside top-tier text processing throughput. Multi-core compute, uncached memory bandwidth, and transactional benchmarks such as Redis and static web serving deliver steady mid-range throughput. The dedicated core allocation eliminates shared-host contention, making this instance well suited for production databases, compilation clusters, continuous integration pipelines, and application backends requiring consistent processing capacity.
